records.d: Alessandro Volta built the pile in 1800: the first battery. The current flowed chemically. The storage was invented.
records.h: Stacked zinc and copper discs with brine produced steady current. The battery was born. The storage was chemical.
records.mj: Established - documented 1800 Volta pile; first battery.

records.d: Gaston Plante invented the lead-acid battery in 1859: the first rechargeable. The battery could refill. The storage was reusable.
records.h: Lead plates in sulfuric acid stored and released charge reversibly. The car would use it. The recharge was invented.
records.mj: Established - documented 1859 Plante; first rechargeable battery.

records.d: Waldemar Jungner invented nickel-cadmium in 1899: the portable rechargeable. The battery went mobile. The storage traveled.
records.h: NiCd chemistry powered portable devices for a century. The toxicity was the cost. The mobile was the benefit.
records.mj: Established - documented 1899 Jungner; nickel-cadmium battery.

records.d: Stanley Whittingham developed lithium intercalation in the 1970s: the lithium battery's foundation. The Nobel came in 2019. The chemistry was the future.
records.h: Titanium disulfide cathodes intercalated lithium. The concept was revolutionary. The future was lithium.
records.mj: Established - documented Whittingham work; 2019 Nobel Prize.

records.d: John Goodenough's cobalt-oxide cathode in 1980 made Li-ion practical: the battery that powers the world. The cathode was the key. The Nobel came in 2019.
records.h: LiCoO2 doubled the voltage. The chemistry was commercializable. The world would run on it.
records.mj: Established - documented 1980 Goodenough cathode; 2019 Nobel Prize.
records.t: 1980: the Cathode That Powers the World

records.d: Akira Yoshino built the first modern Li-ion prototype in 1985: the safe rechargeable. The battery was commercializable. The Nobel came in 2019.
records.h: Carbon anode with Goodenough cathode made a safe cell. The prototype was the product. The trio won.
records.mj: Established - documented 1985 Yoshino prototype; 2019 Nobel Prize.

records.d: Sony commercialized Li-ion in 1991: the battery went mass-market. The camcorder powered. The era began.
records.h: The first commercial cells powered electronics. The market was created. The era was lithium.
records.mj: Established - documented 1991 Sony commercialization; first Li-ion products.

records.d: Lithium iron phosphate in 1996 made Li-ion safe and cheap: the workhorse chemistry. The battery got practical. The EV would use it.
records.h: LiFePO4 offered safety and longevity. The chemistry was the workhorse. The EV adopted it.
records.mj: Established - documented 1996 LiFePO4; safe Li-ion chemistry.

records.d: The Tesla Roadster shipped in 2008: the Li-ion sports car. The battery went fast. The EV was desirable.
records.h: Thousands of laptop cells powered a sports car. The proof was performance. The desirable was electric.
records.mj: Established - documented 2008 Roadster; Li-ion electric sports car.

records.d: Li-ion costs collapsed in the 2010s: 90% cheaper. The battery got affordable. The EV went mainstream.
records.h: Scale and learning drove prices from $1,000 to $100/kWh. The collapse was historic. The mainstream was electric.
records.mj: Established - documented cost decline; Li-ion learning curve.
